target_customer: Academic researchers and students who pay for AI literature search
problem: General chatbots lack current information and peer-reviewed citations, and classic academic search leaves researchers reading many papers by hand.

founders.name: Eshan Agarwal
previous_startups: Planar (GitHub code review integration, shut down July 2023 and pivoted into Epsilon)
founders.background_notes: His own post says he and his cofounder were software engineers at Big Tech companies, without naming them. Education not found.

founders.name: Viraj Rai
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by a secondary article only; the YC page lists no founders. Background not found.

exit.reason: Not public. The company website carries a notice that the product will shut down on April 30, 2026, with no stated cause.

technical_complexity.rationale: A retrieval and summarization layer over public paper indexes such as Semantic Scholar, built with GPT-4 class models in 2023, which two engineers could ship. The hard parts were citation accuracy and index freshness.

defensibility.rationale: It relied on third party paper indexes and third party models, so any similar tool could be copied in weeks and nothing in the sources points to lock in or proprietary data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources. The company later announced its own shutdown for April 2026.

market_need_then: The YC page argues that general LLMs lack up to date information and peer-reviewed citations, and that academic search leaves hours of paper reading. The founder post says a contact asked for help extracting insights from hundreds of scientific papers, which led to the idea.

branding.domain_note: Uses epsilon-ai.com with a suffix, not an exact .com, per the company site.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and promotional, focused on saving time: cut twenty hours of research to twenty minutes.

brand_strength.rationale: Epsilon is a common word shared with a large marketing firm and a Greek letter, and searches returned only directory listings and one tools blog, with no press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: Planar, a GitHub integration for faster code review
pivots.to: Epsilon, AI search over scientific papers
pivots.why: Product led growth hit security reviews of source code access, engineering managers did not want code review tools, and a contact asked for help with scientific papers (founder post, year inferred from its February 2024 date).

outcome_analysis: Epsilon began as Planar, a code review tool that failed to find revenue, and pivoted in mid 2023 to AI academic search shortly after Demo Day. No funding was found in any source. The company site now announces a shutdown on April 30, 2026, but no source states why, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. Thin defensibility and a crowded field of AI research tools are plausible contributors, but no source supports them.
notes: The directory lists status Active, but the company website (fetched in November 2026) states a shutdown on April 30, 2026; a web search did not corroborate it, so treat the exit as single sourced. Searches for dated competitors near mid 2023 returned only undated directory pages, so the list is empty. The YC page says founded 2022, a secondary source says 2023. Co-founder Viraj Rai is named only by a secondary article.
